record.paper_title: Status, open problems and prospects of the decay B+ → ℓ+νℓ
record.original_question: Can SuperB-era analyses reduce the dominant irreducible systematic uncertainty in BR(B+ → τ+ντ), mainly from Btag and Bsig reconstruction efficiencies and B Bbar counting, enough to avoid a systematics-dominated measurement and reach the assumed factor-of-two improvement that would give about 4.5% uncertainty at 75 ab−1?

evidence.quote: The irreducible systematic uncertainties on BR(B+ → τ+ντ ) (mainly due to Btag and Bsig reconstruction efficiencies and BB¯ counting) is 8.7%, which is currently a factor of ∼ 2 smaller than the statistical error. It is evident that this measurement will be systematic dominated in the near future if no effort is made to reduce the systematic error. The uncertainty will saturate at ∼ 9% already at ∼ 50 ab−1, which is only 2/3 of the total expected dataset of SuperB.

It is then assumed that the systematic uncertainty can be reduced by a factor of two, which can be considered as a moderately conservative scenario. Under this hypothesis, we obtain the top-left plot of figure 1, where we show the statistical significance as a function of the integrated luminosity, which gives an uncertainty of 4.5% at 75 ab−1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the leptonic decay $B^+ 	o 	au^+ 
u_	au$ measured at a future high-luminosity asymmetric $e^+e^-$ B-factory operating at the $\Upsilon(4S)$ resonance, in which one $B$ meson of the produced $B ar{B}$ pair is fully reconstructed in a hadronic or semileptonic mode (the "tag side", $B_{m tag}$) and the signal $B$ ($B_{m sig}$) is searched for through its leptonic decay. Suppose that, with current analysis techniques, the irreducible systematic uncertainty on the measured branching ratio $\mathrm{BR}(B^+ 	o 	au^+ 
u_	au)$ is $\sigma_{m syst} = 8.7\%$, dominated by three contributions: (i) the $B_{m tag}$ reconstruction efficiency, (ii) the $B_{m sig}$ reconstruction efficiency, and (iii) the $B ar{B}$ counting uncertainty. The statistical uncertainty scales as $1/\sqrt{\mathcal{L}}$ with integrated luminosity $\mathcal{L}$. Under the hypothesis that improved analysis techniques, control samples, and detector understanding allow each of these systematic components to be reduced so that the total irreducible systematic uncertainty on $\mathrm{BR}(B^+	o	au^+
u_	au)$ is reduced by a factor of two (to roughly $4.35\%$), determine whether the combined statistical-plus-systematic uncertainty on $\mathrm{BR}(B^+	o	au^+
u_	au)$ at an integrated luminosity of $\mathcal{L} = 75\ \mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ can be brought down to approximately $4.5\%$ without becoming systematics-dominated, and identify which improvements in the calibration and modeling of $B_{m tag}$ efficiency, $B_{m sig}$ efficiency, and $B ar{B}$ counting are required to realize this scenario.
artifact.status_search_result: SuperB was cancelled, but Belle II at SuperKEKB pursues the same measurement program. As of 2025, Belle II reported a hadronic-tag measurement of $B^+\to\tau^+\nu_\tau$ with 387M $B\bar B$ pairs giving a 3.0σ evidence and systematic uncertainty around 15%, still statistics-limited. Whether systematic uncertainties can be halved to reach ~4.5% total uncertainty at 75 ab$^{-1}$ has not been definitively demonstrated; Belle II strategy documents continue to project significant but not yet achieved reductions, so the question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of B+→τ+ν_τ branching fraction with a hadronic tagging method at Belle II
status_evidence.snippet: Belle II measurement using 387M BB pairs reports BR=(1.24±0.41±0.19)×10^-4, evidence at 3σ, statistics-limited.
status_evidence.claim: Current Belle II measurement is still statistics-limited and far from the projected ~4.5% total uncertainty regime.

status_evidence.title: The Belle II Experiment at SuperKEKB (European Strategy input 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Belle II projections to multi-ab^-1 luminosities discuss systematic-reduction programs for tag-side and BBbar counting.
status_evidence.claim: Reaching ~4.5% uncertainty at 75 ab^-1 requires factor-of-two systematic reduction; not yet demonstrated.
